Parmashta
par-MASH-tah
n. (proper name; a son of Haman)
Persian, perhaps the strongest or superior; the sense is uncertain.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

Parmashta is the seventh named of the ten sons of Haman. “And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha” (Esther 9:9) close the list. After the first day's fighting the king reported to Esther, “The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman” (Esther 9:12), and asked her further petition. She asked for one more day in Shushan, “and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows” (Esther 9:13). “And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons” (Esther 9:14). Haman had boasted to his wife and friends of the multitude of his children; that multitude ended on the gallows he built for Mordecai. Parmashta's name survives only in the record of his house's fall, a witness that the LORD keeps His promise to curse those who curse the seed of Abraham.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Parmashta is a Persian proper name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Parmashta is a Persian proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears once, in Esther 9:9.

He was a son of Haman.

He was slain in Shushan with his brothers.

He was hanged on the gallows at Esther's request.

Key Scripture

Est 9:9 — "And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,"

Est 9:12 — "And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done."

Est 9:13 — "Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows."

Est 9:14 — "And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons."

Modern Corruption

Haman's boast in many sons is counted as security; his ten sons, Parmashta among them, were hanged on the gallows.

expand to see more

The book of Esther records the death of Haman's sons without apology, and modern readers often recoil. The decree of Haman had armed the empire to destroy every Jew, man, woman and child, and the sons stood with their father. The Jews fought in self-defense and, as the text notes, laid not their hand on the spoil.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God turns the wicked device back upon the head of its author, and preserves His people when all seems lost.
